The Gradient of the Jeffreys Penalty in the Joint Vector

Source: R/jfp_engine.R
jfp_gradient.Rd

Computes \(\partial_k\sum_b a_b\log|\tilde I_b|\) over every coordinate of \(u\).

Usage

jfp_gradient(st)

Arguments

st

A state, from jfp_state().

Value

A numeric vector over \(u\).

Details

For a block whose rows do not move, $$\partial_k\log|\tilde I| = \mathrm{tr}(\tilde I^{-1}\partial_k\tilde I) = \sum_t w_t\sum_c V_{c,t,k}\,s_{c,t},\qquad s_{c,t} = -\sum_{q,r}h_{qr,t}\,\partial_{\eta_c}E_{qr,t},$$ with \(V_{c,t,k}\) the derivative of the predictor of equation \(c\) in \(u_k\) and \(\partial_{\eta_c}E_{qr}\) from distributions7::distrib_dexpected_hessian(). This is the contraction of u_vector() with the block's leverages in place of the diagonal of a matrix over \(u\), which cannot hold the constant direction.

See also

jfp_value(), jfp_hessian()
